headline: The US transport department has granted self-driving truck company Aurora a five-year exemption from warning-device rules.
score_reason: Stays at pool 6: an official decision with a clear legal effect, which the regulator can revoke.
importance_line: What changed: self-driving trucks now have a five-year route around the rule that a driver must place warning devices, which matters to road users and to truck firms; the doubt: the exemption can be revoked, and Aurora runs only about 20 trucks on public roads today.
summary: Reuters reports that the US Department of Transportation approved, late on 7 Oct 2026, a five-year exemption for Aurora and other self-driving truck companies from the rule that drivers place warning devices around a stopped truck, letting them use beacons mounted on the truck cab instead. Aurora, which runs about 20 self-driving trucks on public roads, had applied for the five-year exemption in April, and the agency says it would revoke an exemption if safety fell below earlier levels.
